question: How much lighter is the multilayer urea crystal with both layers at 400 °C than the single-layer standard group 2 crystal at 400 °C?
rendered:
To answer this question, we need to look at the mass of the multilayer urea crystal with both layers at 400 °C and the mass of the single-layer standard group 2 crystal at 400 °C.

The mass of the single-layer standard group 2 crystal at 400 °C is 1.118 g (Table 3).

The mass of the multilayer urea crystal with both layers at 400 °C is 1.055 g (Table 7).

To find the difference, we subtract the mass of the multilayer crystal from the mass of the single-layer crystal:

1.118 g - 1.055 g = 0.063 g

So, the multilayer urea crystal with both layers at 400 °C is 0.063 g lighter than the single-layer standard group 2 crystal at 400 °C.
